programme.title: Rad: Lombardei-Rundfahrt
programme.desc: Nach seinem Sturz bei der Vuelta konnte Tadej Pogacar beim fünften Radsport-Monument des Jahres nicht antreten. programme.title: Radsport: Cycling Show
programme.desc: "Cycling Show" informiert über die aktuellen Themen und Entwicklungen sowie über die anstehenden Top-Rennen in der Profi-Radsportwelt. Moderiert wird die Sendung von Radsportlegende Sir Bradley Wiggins, fünfacher Olympiasieger und Tour-de-France Gewinner von 2012. Unterstützt wird der 44-Jährige dabei von Sportjournalist Graham Willgoss.

programme.title: Snooker: WM
programme.desc: Im Finale standen sich der Chinese Wu Yize und der Engländer Shaun Murphy gegenüber. Der 22-jährige chinesische Shootingstar besiegte den Briten in einer Partie voller Wendungen mit 18:17 und wurde damit der zweitjüngste Snooker-Weltmeister der Geschichte. Die Weltmeisterschaft war der abschließende Wettbewerb der Saison 2025/26. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Blue Hens vs Raiders ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Colgate Raiders navigate to the Bob Carpenter Center for an NCAA men's basketball battle with the Delaware Blue Hens. The Hens, sitting at 1-2, hope to establish home rhythm against a winless Raiders squad hungry for a breakthrough. Guard C. Bailey III fuels Delaware with 24 points per game on scorching 65.4% shooting, while Colgate’s Alex Alekseyenko provides a consistent spark with a double-double average for an offense ranking first in scoring efficiency.

programme.title: Bills at Jets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Buffalo Bills, a powerhouse with a pristine 4-0 road record and a league-best 256 points, storm into MetLife Stadium to face the reeling New York Jets, who have lost seven of nine and sit at 2-7. Boasting the top-ranked offense averaging 400 yards per game, the Bills excel in the red zone at an 80.95% clip, while Josh Allen has amassed 2,027 passing yards alongside 12 touchdowns through the air and a staggering nine on the ground. The Jets, anchored by a defense that leads the NFL in forced fumbles with 13, rely on Aaron Rodgers’ 2,078 passing yards and Garrett Wilson’s 527 receiving yards, though the club struggles to stop the run as Buffalo’s James Cook churns out 814 rushing yards. This AFC East rivalry heats up with the Bills dominating the series, and New York’s slim playoff hopes hinge on snapping a skid against a fellow division foe that tops the conference standings.

programme.title: Chiefs at Falcons ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Kansas City Chiefs, boasting a stellar 6-2 mark and leading their division, storm into Mercedes-Benz Stadium to battle the reeling 3-6 Atlanta Falcons, who have lost four of five at home. KC's offense, piloted by Patrick Mahomes (2,037 yards, 14 TDs) and featuring the punishing ground game of Kenneth Walker III (872 yards, 7 scores), ranks fourth in yards per game, while Atlanta's defense has been gashed, surrendering 384 yards per contest. The Falcons, anchored by Bijan Robinson's 880 rushing yards, have a -8 turnover differential and are dead last in interception percentage, woes that Mahomes’s crisp 101.8 rating will exploit. This NFC-AFC clash sees the Chiefs riding a wave of momentum as heavy favorites, while the Falcons seek to salvage a spiraling campaign in front of their faithful.

programme.desc: The visiting Detroit Pistons, leading this NBA series 1-0, visit Kaseya Center to face Miami Heat (5-6). The 7-3 Pistons, top in blocks and steals, meet the Heat's second-ranked assists, driven by Antetokounmpo's 27.7 points and 12.6 rebounds; Cunningham's 22.3 points and 7.6 assists lead. Despite home court, the Pistons are favorites, their form and series lead ominous.

programme.title: Rams at Cardinals ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The red-hot Los Angeles Rams storm into State Farm Stadium for an NFC West grudge match with the scuffling Arizona Cardinals. Holding a strong 5-4 record, Matthew Stafford (16 TDs), Kyren Williams (6 rushing scores), and Puka Nacua (715 yards) lead a high-powered attack for the NFL playoff push. The 3-6 Cardinals, averaging just 19.8 points, rely on Jacoby Brissett's 10 touchdown passes and Trey McBride's 5 scores to turn their season around at home.

programme.title: Flames at Ducks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Calgary Flames hit the Honda Center ice trailing the Anaheim Ducks 2-1 in their series, needing a win to even the aggregate score on the road. Anaheim, leading the NHL with a blistering 38.5 power-play, boasts Leo Carlsson’s 26 points and Cutter Gauthier’s 15 goals, while the Flames rely on Joel Farabee’s team-leading 17 points and solid .914 save percentage from Dustin Cooley. Calgary’s middling 8-9-1 record places them near the bottom of the league standings, but their 6-3-1 recent form suggests they can challenge a Ducks squad that sits fourth in goals despite owning the league’s worst save percentage (.869) and a depleted crease, with Laurent Brossoit and Ville Husso struggling. This Pacific Division clash at Anaheim’s fortress carries extra weight as a special milestone—a pivotal tilt for a Flames club desperate to snap a five-game road losing streak.

programme.title: Timberwolves vs Bulls ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Minnesota Timberwolves, sitting atop the NBA’s Northwest Division with an 8-3 record, host the struggling Chicago Bulls, who are languishing near the basement at 1-8, in this opening series matchup at Target Center. Riding a formidable 7-3 stretch, the Wolves boast the league’s top rebounding rate and a potent offense spearheaded by Anthony Edwards’ blistering 4.5 triples per game, while Rudy Gobert anchors the paint with 12.1 boards nightly. Conversely, the Bulls, losers of eight of their last ten, are paced by guard Josh Giddey’s 8.4 assists per contest, but face a daunting task against Minnesota’s stifling defense, which ranks first in defensive rebounds and third in steals. This contest marks the kickoff of a new series, with the Timberwolves heavily favored given their dominant home court and Chicago’s inability to generate consistent stops on the road.

programme.title: Trailblazers vs Eagles ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Nearing the end of a grueling NCAA Football campaign, Eastern Washington Eagles bring a grim 2-8 record into Greater Zion Stadium for a showdown with the lowly 1-9 Utah Tech Trailblazers. This clash of desperate cellar-dwellers features starkly contrasting offensive engines: Eagles dual-threat QB N. Bell is a statistical machine with 20 passing TDs and 9 rushing scores despite a league-worst 40 sacks, while Trailblazer rusher A. Chatman's 5 rushing touchdowns serve as a lone home bright spot.

programme.title: Celtics vs Mavericks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Boston Celtics, boasting a league-best 10-2 record and a perfect 5-0 home mark, welcome the Dallas Mavericks (7-5) to TD Garden for this NBA series opener. Riding a 9-1 surge, the C's lead the league in effective field goal and three-point percentage, fueled by Jayson Tatum's 26.3 PPG and Paul George's 2.1 steals. However, Dallas counters with Cooper Flagg (24.6 PPG, 6.5 APG) and a top-five block attack. The Celtics enter as heavy favorites, while the Mavs aim to improve their 2-3 road record and snap Boston's home dominance.

programme.title: Steelers at Bengals ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Pittsburgh Steelers, boasting a strong 6-2 record, roll into Paycor Stadium for a bitter AFC North rivalry clash with the 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals, who are red-hot with the league’s top-ranked passing attack led by Joe Burrow’s 20 touchdowns and a 111.6 rating. The Bengals, nailing a perfect 100% field goal percentage and averaging 29.4 points per game, face a Steelers defense that leads the NFL with 26 sacks, anchored by T.J. Watt’s 7.5 sacks, while Burrow’s favorite target Tee Higgins has racked up 726 receiving yards. Pittsburgh counters with Jaylen Warren’s 704 rushing yards and a plus-five turnover differential, though Cincy’s opportunistic D has forced 10 fumbles, setting the stage for a pivotal divisional showdown at a venue where the home crowd could tip the scales.

programme.title: Rams vs Tigers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The undefeated and favored Rhode Island Rams, boasting a spotless 4-0 record, welcome the Princeton Tigers (3-1) to the Thomas M. Ryan Center for a pivotal NCAA clash. URI's high-powered offense, averaging over 81 points, relies on M. Deniusas's 14.0 scoring average and J. Fontenet II's relentless 8.2 rebounds per game. Countering for Princeton is the versatile J. Hicke, stuffing the stat sheet with 12.8 points, 6.5 boards, and 4.0 assists nightly. Both squads enter with sharp form, setting the stage for a compelling test of styles.

programme.title: Oilers at Flyers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The NHL-leading Edmonton Oilers, boasting a scorching 14-3-3 record and a dominant 7-0-1 road mark, aim to extend their series lead over the Philadelphia Flyers to 2-0 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Connor McDavid, who has already amassed a staggering 49 points, drives an offense that leads the league in goals, while the Flyers, languishing in the basement at 5-10-6, counter with rookie phenom Matvei Michkov and his team-best 10 goals. Philadelphia’s defense blocks the most shots in the league yet owns the worst goal differential, a glaring issue against Edmonton’s red-hot power play, which converts at a stellar 33.3%.

programme.title: Canucks at Golden Knights ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Vegas Golden Knights, leading the series 1-0, welcome the struggling Vancouver Canucks to T-Mobile Arena. VGK sit near the top of the NHL standings with a 13-5-2 record, while the Canucks have lost nine of their last ten. Jack Eichel (26 points) and Mark Stone (10 goals) power Vegas’ offense, but Vancouver’s Elias Pettersson (21 points) tries to spark a squad that ranks dead last in goals against (4.52 per game). These Pacific Division rivals meet again after Vegas took Game 1, hoping to extend their home dominance (7-3-1). VGK’s power play clicks at 27.4%, while VAN’s penalty kill is a league-worst 62.7%.

programme.title: Jaguars vs Trojans ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Troy Trojans travel to Hancock Whitney Stadium to clash with the South Alabama Jaguars in this pivotal Sun Belt rivalry showdown, as both teams sit at 4-5 overall and 2-3 in league play, fighting to stay bowl-eligible. The Jags boast a formidable ground attack, ranking 19th nationally with 1,864 rushing yards behind the bruising backfield duo of K. Phillips (595 yards, six touchdowns) and P. Martin (589 yards, seven scores), while Troy counters with a defense that has forced 16 takeaways, keyed by K. Jones’ 70 tackles and J. Powe’s three interceptions. South Alabama has been a fortress at home with a 3-1 record, averaging a blistering 32.4 points per game, but the Trojans have a knack for creating chaos, logging 10 forced fumbles and generating a plus-one turnover differential. This marks a critical milestone for both programs as they chase postseason eligibility, with the Jaguars looking to extend their home dominance in the series.

programme.title: Timberwolves vs Bulls ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Minnesota Timberwolves, sitting atop the NBA’s Northwest Division with an 8-3 record, host the struggling Chicago Bulls, who are languishing near the basement at 1-8, in this opening series matchup at Target Center. Riding a formidable 7-3 stretch, the Wolves boast the league’s top rebounding rate and a potent offense spearheaded by Anthony Edwards’ blistering 4.5 triples per game, while Rudy Gobert anchors the paint with 12.1 boards nightly. Conversely, the Bulls, losers of eight of their last ten, are paced by guard Josh Giddey’s 8.4 assists per contest, but face a daunting task against Minnesota’s stifling defense, which ranks first in defensive rebounds and third in steals. This contest marks the kickoff of a new series, with the Timberwolves heavily favored given their dominant home court and Chicago’s inability to generate consistent stops on the road.

programme.title: Bobcats vs Mustangs ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Montana State Bobcats greet the Cal Poly Mustangs at Worthington Arena. Both sides have struggled early, the Bobcats at 1-2 and the Mustangs at 2-2. Cal Poly’s offense, averaging 79 points, is spearheaded by guard H. Mousa’s 20.8 points per game, while Montana State counters with J. Davis’s 16 points and 5.7 rebounds. The Bobcats, buoyed by a home record of 1-0, look to tighten their defense against a Mustangs side that turns the ball over 17.8 times a contest.

The visitors, bearing a 3-1 record, present a high-scoring offense averaging 93.5, orchestrated by K. Sanders' 20.2 points and disrupted by G. Best's 4.8 steals. The resident Tigers, standing firm at 2-1, draw strength from their rebounding, a pillar led by G. Ripp's 10.7 boards. This NCAA clash fascinatingly contrasts a soaring offense with a steadfast home defense.

programme.title: Kings vs Thunder ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Oklahoma City Thunder, boasting an 8-4 record and riding solid form, head to Golden 1 Center to open their series against the struggling Sacramento Kings, who sit at 1-10 and have dropped nine of their last ten. The Thunder rely on superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (30.5 PPG) and rebounder Isaiah Hartenstein (10.5 RPG), while the Kings counter with Duane Acuff Jr.’s scoring (25.4 PPG) and Domantas Sabonis’ double-double threat. OKC dominates the standings, and the Kings' 0-7 home mark spells trouble in this NBA matchup.

programme.title: Trailblazers vs Eagles ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Nearing the end of a grueling NCAA Football campaign, Eastern Washington Eagles bring a grim 2-8 record into Greater Zion Stadium for a showdown with the lowly 1-9 Utah Tech Trailblazers. This clash of desperate cellar-dwellers features starkly contrasting offensive engines: Eagles dual-threat QB N. Bell is a statistical machine with 20 passing TDs and 9 rushing scores despite a league-worst 40 sacks, while Trailblazer rusher A. Chatman's 5 rushing touchdowns serve as a lone home bright spot.

programme.title: Eagles vs Crimson ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Harvard Crimson, boasting a 2-1 record, invade Bender Arena to duel the American University Eagles, who enter at 1-2 on their home hardwood. American’s engine is guard M. Collins, averaging 22.0 points, while Harvard forward T. Batties III anchors the interior with 1.8 blocks per game. The Eagles have struggled defensively, ranking near the bottom in steals, but Harvard’s frigid 27.4% three-point shooting offers a reprieve. Both NCAA squads aim to steady their early-season form in this non-conference clash.

programme.desc: At Tulsa’s H. A. Chapman Stadium, a Hurricane of momentum, the Golden Hurricane boast a formidable 33.1 points per game while the Florida Atlantic Owls, soaring at 40.2, lead the NCAA Football scoring charts. FAU’s aerial assault, anchored by quarterback C. Veltkamp with 27 touchdowns and wide receiver E. Messer’s 983 yards and 12 scores, contrasts with Tulsa’s rushing duo of D. Alston and T. Jones, who have combined for 913 yards and 11 touchdowns. The Owls, riding a 6-3 record, have lost three away games yet are potent with a league-best 4 return touchdowns, including 2 on kickoffs, while Tulsa’s 5-4 form shows defensive resilience with 24 sacks and 8 fumble recoveries. This rivalry clash finds FAU with a superior 3-2 conference mark, hosting significant implications for the standings as Tulsa clings to a 76% win probability at their home venue.

programme.title: Terriers vs Big Green ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: At Case Gym, the Boston University Terriers, boasting a formidable 3-1 record, prepare to host a Dartmouth Big Green squad fresh off an undefeated two-game road swing, their own 3-1 start a testament to their resilience. BU’s K. Alexander, averaging 18.8 points, orchestrates the offense against a Dartmouth side that launches 31.8 three-point attempts per game, with C. McNamee leading the charge at 14.5 points. The Terriers’ 52.1% field goal shooting, top-40 nationally, faces a Big Green defense that ranks 47th in steals, setting the stage for a pivotal NCAA clash. Both teams carry identical 3-1 marks into this non-conference battle, where home-court advantage and the rivalry’s history amplify the stakes.

UTM's balanced 2-2 start has produced a dominant 340-54 aggregate scoring edge, making them heavy favorites against the winless Royals. The Royals lean on C. Rogers' 4.0 assists to counter a stifling home defense.

programme.title: Wizards vs Rockets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Houston Rockets (10-3) visit the Washington Wizards (4-9) at Capital One Arena in an NBA matchup. The Rockets enter with a 7-3 record over their last ten games, while the Wizards have lost eight of ten. This begins the season series between the clubs. Alperen Sengun (23.1 PPG, 9.6 RPG, 7.6 APG) leads Houston's attack, and Anthony Davis (25.6 PPG, 10.5 RPG) is the go-to for Washington. Houston is sixth in scoring and fourth in field goal percentage, while Washington ranks second in defensive rebounds and blocks. The Rockets sit near the top of the West standings, with the Wizards near the bottom of the East.

programme.title: Gauchos vs Bobcats ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: High in the coastal California air, the UC Santa Barbara Gauchos, undefeated with a pristine 3-0 record, prepare to defend their Thunderdome home court against the visiting UC Merced Bobcats in this NCAA Men’s Basketball clash. The Gauchos arrive with a staggering 99.9 percent win probability, their offense ranking third nationally in three-point accuracy (52.1 percent) and first in points per possession, as guard V. Vartiainen leads the scoring charge with 14 points per game. While the Bobcats are without a major player, UCSB brings a 2.4 assist-to-turnover ratio and a rivalry-fueled advantage, aiming to extend their perfect start in a venue where they have dominated historically.

programme.title: Grizzlies vs Nets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Memphis Grizzlies (8-4) host the Brooklyn Nets (3-8) at FedExForum in this NBA series game. The Grizzlies, 6-4 in their last ten, are favorites at home despite a 2-4 home record. The Nets have gone 3-7 recently. Ty Jerome (25.4 PPG) leads Memphis, while Michael Porter Jr. (21.5 PPG) leads Brooklyn. Memphis tops the league in free throw percentage (85.3%) and effective FG%, while Brooklyn commits the most turnovers. This second series matchup sees the Grizzlies aiming to build on their strong form.

programme.title: Pelicans vs Nuggets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Denver Nuggets, holding a 2-0 series lead, visit the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center. The 6-4 Nuggets boast elite playmaking with the league’s top assist ratio, powered by Nikola Jokic’s near triple-double averages (23.5 PPG, 10.8 RPG, 9.0 APG) and Jamal Murray’s 26.2 PPG. New Orleans, struggling at 4-9, ranks second in steals and first in free throws made and points in paint, fueled by Zion Williamson’s 21.8 PPG and 2.1 SPG. Denver’s superior form (6-4 last ten) contrasts with the Pelicans’ 4-6 slide, making the Nuggets clear favorites.

programme.title: Explorers vs Owls ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Here, in the John Glaser Arena, the Temple Owls advance into the territory of their North Philadelphia NCAA rivals, the La Salle Explorers. The Owls arrive as favorites, wielding a superior 1-1 record against La Salle's 1-2, and a clean disciplinary slate against La Salle's single disqualification. Temple fields the formidable rebounder B. Njie, while La Salle counters with the orchestrator J. Johnson and the prolific scoring of K. Burton. Turnovers heavily fracture the offensive rhythm in this desperate struggle for hardwood dominance.

programme.title: Grizzlies vs Nets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Memphis Grizzlies (8-4) host the Brooklyn Nets (3-8) at FedExForum in this NBA series game. The Grizzlies, 6-4 in their last ten, are favorites at home despite a 2-4 home record. The Nets have gone 3-7 recently. Ty Jerome (25.4 PPG) leads Memphis, while Michael Porter Jr. (21.5 PPG) leads Brooklyn. Memphis tops the league in free throw percentage (85.3%) and effective FG%, while Brooklyn commits the most turnovers. This second series matchup sees the Grizzlies aiming to build on their strong form.

programme.title: Predators at Sharks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Nashville Predators, apex hunters boasting an 11-4-5 record and dominant 8-1-1 recent form, venture into the San Jose Sharks’ SAP Center. The Sharks, languishing at 9-11-2, cling to their 1-0 series lead. San Jose’s defense, ranking first in NHL saves, revolves around Macklin Celebrini's eight goals. Nashville counters with a peerless penalty kill, orchestrated by Roman Josi (21 assists) and Steven Stamkos (11 goals). This pivotal home-ice clash deepens their fierce rivalry.

programme.title: Cavaliers vs Mavericks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Cleveland Cavaliers welcome the Dallas Mavericks to Rocket Arena for the series opener in this NBA clash. Cleveland's top-ranked offense (116.4 PPG, league-high 183 threes) contrasts with their 4-6 recent form, while Dallas arrives with a 6-4 run. Cooper Flagg (24.6 PPG, 6.5 APG) leads the visitors, and the Cavs counter with Donovan Mitchell (23.0 PPG) and Jarrett Allen's inside presence. With elite defensive rebounding and a strong assist game, Cleveland is favored at home, though both teams sit near .500.

programme.title: Flames at Ducks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Calgary Flames hit the Honda Center ice trailing the Anaheim Ducks 2-1 in their series, needing a win to even the aggregate score on the road. Anaheim, leading the NHL with a blistering 38.5 power-play, boasts Leo Carlsson’s 26 points and Cutter Gauthier’s 15 goals, while the Flames rely on Joel Farabee’s team-leading 17 points and solid .914 save percentage from Dustin Cooley. Calgary’s middling 8-9-1 record places them near the bottom of the league standings, but their 6-3-1 recent form suggests they can challenge a Ducks squad that sits fourth in goals despite owning the league’s worst save percentage (.869) and a depleted crease, with Laurent Brossoit and Ville Husso struggling. This Pacific Division clash at Anaheim’s fortress carries extra weight as a special milestone—a pivotal tilt for a Flames club desperate to snap a five-game road losing streak.

programme.title: Lakers vs Hornets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The surging Lakers, boasting a 9-2 record atop the West, welcome the struggling Hornets to crypto.com Arena as this new series ignites; Los Angeles paces the league with 121.9 points per game, a dominant stat fueled by Luka Doncic’s staggering 39.3 PPG average, while Charlotte, languishing at 3-7 and 30th in scoring, must counter Walker Kessler’s interior presence and league-best offensive rebounding. The purple and gold have won eight of ten entering this clash, sitting comfortably near the conference summit, but the Hornets’ 52.7 rebound rate could exploit a Laker squad ranked 29th in total boards. An iconic non-conference rivalry adds extra juice to this marquee matchup at the iconic LA venue.

programme.title: Screaming Eagles vs Broncos ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Western Michigan Broncos, riding high on a 3-1 record, storm into Liberty Arena to face the 1-3 Southern Indiana Screaming Eagles in this non-conference clash. The Eagles have been dominant on the glass, ranking 11th nationally in rebounds per game, while the Broncos boast the nation’s third-best offensive rebounding percentage. Western Michigan’s backcourt catalyst is J. Washington, averaging 12.2 points and 3.8 assists, while Stephen Yamanouchi-Williams anchors the paint for So Indiana with 7.2 boards and 1.2 blocks per contest. The Screaming Eagles are desperate to protect their home floor after starting 1-3, but the Broncos aim to exploit a subpar Southern Indiana defense that surrenders 78 points per game.

programme.title: Panthers at Stars ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the American Airlines Center, a compelling NHL series continues for the structured Dallas Stars against the visiting Florida Panthers, a whirlwind of league-leading penalty minutes and hits. The Stars rely on superb form, epitomized by goalie Oettinger and his milestone four shutouts. Their faceoff dominance meets the Panthers' raw aggression in this absorbing rivalry. The home favorites aim to maintain their aggregate standing over such vibrant, undisciplined chaos.

programme.title: Patriots at Lions ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The 6-2 Detroit Lions, boasting an NFL-best 27 sacks and a perfect 4-0 home record, host the 5-4 New England Patriots at FC Bayern Munich Stadium in a clash of conference leaders. Detroit’s Jared Goff is on fire with a 106.5 rating and 15 touchdowns against just 2 picks, but the Patriots counter with Drake Maye’s 18 scoring strikes despite his 11 interceptions. The Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs has ripped off 847 rushing yards and 9 scores behind a unit ranking 3rd in yards per game, while New England’s defense, tied for 2nd in the league with 25 sacks, looks to exploit a Lions crew that averages 27.8 points. This rivalry reunion sees the Patriots, however, struggling with a league-worst -11 turnover differential and 19 giveaways.

programme.title: Suns vs Lakers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the vast arena of the NBA, the league-leading Los Angeles Lakers, boasting an 11-2 record and the top-scoring offense, descend upon the Mortgage Matchup Center to face the Phoenix Suns, who sit at 5-6 and are opening this series on their home floor. The Suns’ defense, ranked 4th in steals, must contend with Luka Doncic, who powers the Lakers’ attack with a staggering 38.6 points per game, while Phoenix relies on Devin Booker’s 25.5 points to spark their 3rd-ranked offense. With the Lakers holding a commanding 6-1 road record and the Suns struggling away from home, this rivalry clash sees Los Angeles as the clear favorite, despite Phoenix’s strong defensive rebounding.

programme.title: Panthers at Saints ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Carolina Panthers, sitting at 3-5, roll into the Caesars Superdome to renew a bitter NFC South rivalry with the equally-matched New Orleans Saints, who also boast a 3-5 record. The Saints have been a turnover machine, leading the league in fumbles lost, yet Bryce Young has been slinging it for 2,197 yards and 16 touchdowns for the Panthers. Chris Hubbard’s 619 ground yards will test a New Orleans defense coming off a tough stretch, while Saints pass-catcher Chris Olave hauls in 56 receptions for 734 yards. This pivotal divisional clash sees the Panthers trying to improve their 1-1 division mark against a Saints squad still winless in their own division at 0-1.

programme.title: Lumberjacks vs Wildcats ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The red-hot Northern Arizona Lumberjacks, boasting an 8-2 record and riding a dominant 4-0 home mark at the J. Lawrence Walkup Skydome, welcome a Weber State Wildcats squad that’s 6-4 but has dropped two of three on the road. This crucial Big Sky clash finds NAU (6-1 in conference) sitting atop the league standings, while the Wildcats (5-2) are nipping at their heels in a fierce rivalry with major postseason implications. The Lumberjacks’ dual-threat QB T. Pennington has racked up 2,320 passing yards and 496 rushing yards with 14 total TDs, but he must beware a stingy Weber St defense that leads the nation with six blocked kicks and has forced 22 takeaways. Meanwhile, Wildcats receiver N. Kjar is on a tear with 902 yards and 11 touchdowns, though his unit’s 13 interceptions thrown could spell trouble against an NAU secondary that’s picked off 12 passes. The previous meeting saw a barnburner, and with both offenses averaging over 32 points per game, expect another classic in Flagstaff.

programme.title: Bucks vs Hawks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Atlanta Hawks, boasting a 7-5 record, visit the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum in this NBA series opener. The Hawks enter as favorites, sitting comfortably above .500, while the Bucks languish at 1-11 with the league's highest turnover rate. Jalen Johnson leads Atlanta with 20 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 7.5 assists per game, and Tyler Herro counters for Milwaukee with 21.6 points. The league leaders in assists and steals, the Hawks look to extend their form, as the Bucks aim to end a disastrous 1-9 stretch.

programme.title: Pelicans vs Nuggets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Denver Nuggets, holding a 2-0 series lead, visit the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center. The 6-4 Nuggets boast elite playmaking with the league’s top assist ratio, powered by Nikola Jokic’s near triple-double averages (23.5 PPG, 10.8 RPG, 9.0 APG) and Jamal Murray’s 26.2 PPG. New Orleans, struggling at 4-9, ranks second in steals and first in free throws made and points in paint, fueled by Zion Williamson’s 21.8 PPG and 2.1 SPG. Denver’s superior form (6-4 last ten) contrasts with the Pelicans’ 4-6 slide, making the Nuggets clear favorites.

programme.title: Lions vs Cougars ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the bustling arena of college basketball, the Loyola Marymount Lions, despite their shaky 1-3 start, prepare to host the Chicago State Cougars at Gersten Pavilion, a fixture that pits two teams with very different recent fortunes against each other. The Cougars, troublemakers with a 2-2 road record and a higher scoring efficiency ranking, arrive in Los Angeles carrying the momentum of a superior form, while the Lions seek redemption on their home court. All eyes are on LMU’s Z. Sensley, a guard averaging a double-double with 17.8 points and 10.5 rebounds, who must contend with Chicago State’s leading scorer, M. Price, who pours in 21.6 points per game. This non-conference battle, significant for both squads aiming to climb the standings, is also a chance for LMU to exploit the Cougars’ defensive frailties, particularly their low block and steal averages.

programme.title: Crusaders vs Great Danes ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The UAlbany Great Danes, boasting a balanced 2-2 record, arrive at the Hart Center Arena to face a winless Holy Cross Crusaders side, still searching for their first victory after three defeats. The Crusaders, anchored at home, struggle offensively with a 36% field goal clip and leaky defense, while the Great Danes showcase a superior 43.8% shooting accuracy and a dominant 5.3 blocks per game, ranking them among the nation’s elite shot-blockers. UAlbany’s O. Engen orchestrates the attack with 18.0 points and 5.7 assists nightly, yet Holy Cross’s forward C. Hare provides a formidable presence with 8.5 rebounds per contest. This NCAA clash sees a desperate Holy Cross attempting to halt their slide against a surging Great Danes outfit.

programme.title: Panthers vs Spartans ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Within the concrete jungle of the GSU Convocation Center, the Georgia State Panthers, overwhelming favorites in this NCAA Men’s Basketball clash, face the wandering Norfolk State Spartans. Despite a stronger 2-2 record, the Spartans must counter the Panthers' imposing aggregate of 343 points anchored by J. Fredson-Cole's double-double prowess and rebounding dominance. Norfolk State counters with their own predator, J. Skyers, whose disruptive 3.3 steals per game threaten to dismantle their hosts' league standing.

The 7-3 Pistons, top in blocks and steals, meet the Heat's second-ranked assists, driven by Antetokounmpo's 27.7 points and 12.6 rebounds; Cunningham's 22.3 points and 7.6 assists lead. Despite home court, the Pistons are favorites, their form and series lead ominous.

programme.title: Seahawks at Raiders ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Seattle Seahawks, sitting at 5-4, roll into Allegiant Stadium to battle the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders in a pivotal AFC-NFC clash. The Silver and Black have leaned heavily on Kirk Cousins, who’s second in the NFL with 20 passing touchdowns and 2,340 yards, but their ground game is dead last at 71.3 yards per game, a glaring weakness against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in tackles for loss. Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba has exploded for 1,036 receiving yards and nine scores, though the Raiders’ defense forces fumbles at a top-two clip and has recovered a league-high seven. The Seahawks boast a strong +1 turnover differential and a more balanced attack, but their 1-2 road record contrasts with Vegas fighting to even their season. This marks a special milestone for the venue, hosting a rare interconference showdown between two storied franchises searching for consistency.

programme.title: Vaqueros vs Lumberjacks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks, a formidable 9-1 squad leading the conference with a 6-1 record, descend upon Robert and Janet Vackar Stadium to face the UTRGV Vaqueros, who sit at 5-5 and 3-4 in league play. SFA’s offense, averaging nearly 40 points per game, is orchestrated by quarterback G. Rutherford, who has amassed 2,374 passing yards and 25 touchdowns, while the Vaqueros’ defense struggles against the pass. The Lumberjacks boast a ferocious pass rush, leading the nation with 40 sacks, anchored by defensive lineman J. Eason with seven, though they will miss injured safety J. Acosta-Lewis, who has only one pick on the season. UTRGV, possessing a 3-1 home record, relies on receiver K. Lee’s 633 yards and six scores, but their secondary, which has intercepted only 15 passes, faces a stern test. This rivalry clash sees SFA as heavy favorites, with the aggregate score from their previous meetings heavily favoring the visitors.

programme.title: Jaguars at Titans ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Jacksonville Jaguars, riding a stellar 6-2 record atop the AFC South, invade Nissan Stadium to face the last-place Tennessee Titans (1-7) in this divisional rivalry. QB Trevor Lawrence torches defenses with 1,932 passing yards and 18 touchdowns, while wideout Parker Washington has five scoring grabs; the Titans' Tony Pollard counters with 595 rushing yards and six scores, but QB C. Ward’s five interceptions, along with a minus-one turnover differential, hinder their cause. Jacksonville’s league-best plus-nine turnover margin and 28.6 points per game underscore their dominant form, leaving Tennessee searching for answers at home.

programme.title: Jazz vs Spurs ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Utah Jazz, enduring a season yielding just one win in twelve, face a relentless predator at the Delta Center: the San Antonio Spurs. Arriving to extend their series lead to two games to nil, the visitors are in devastating form, boasting a perfect ten consecutive victories and a dominant road record. Orchestrating this assault is the titan Victor Wembanyama, whose 28.8 points and league-topping blocks shatter Utah's rhythm. K. George valiantly counters for the Jazz, yet the Spurs' superior precision and defensive dominance leave the home pride fighting for survival in the NBA standings.

programme.title: Bulls vs Golden Griffins ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Buffalo Bulls square off with the Canisius Golden Griffins at Broadview Arena, hosting this NY rivalry clash. Buffalo, entering with a 1-2 record but a perfect 1-0 mark at home, leans on forward A. Lorick III averaging 17 points and a double-double with 10 rebounds per contest. Canisius arrives at 2-2 overall, fueled by guard M. Wilson Jr.’s 18.5 points and dangerous 37.8% three-point shooting as a team. The aggregate score is level, though the Bulls’ swarming defense, tied for 75th with 10.3 steals per game, eyes a milestone home victory against their upstate foes.

programme.title: Vikings at Packers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Green Bay Packers, currently holding a 6-3 record, prepare to host the Minnesota Vikings in a classic NFC North rivalry at Lambeau Field, a venue steeped in history and cherished by all who witness it. The Packers, who lead the league in net passing yards behind the arm of quarterback Jordan Love with his 19 touchdowns, face a Vikings side that boasts a superior 6-2 record and a ferocious pass rush, generating 29 sacks spearheaded by linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel. This encounter marks a crucial clash for divisional supremacy as both teams vie for position in the NFL standings, with the visitors’ turnover differential of plus five contrasting sharply with their hosts’ explosive aerial attack. Wide receiver Christian Watson has been a vital target for the Packers, amassing 879 receiving yards and 7 touchdowns, while the Vikings must contend with the absence of a fully fit secondary after a taxing campaign; the aggregate series score leans heavily toward the home team, yet the Vikings’ disciplined defense, which has forced 13 takeaways, promises a battle of attrition in this historic venue.

programme.title: Thundering Herd vs Mountaineers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: App State Mountaineers visit Marshall Thundering Herd for an NCAA Football rivalry clash at Joan C. Edwards Stadium. Both are 5-4, making this a huge series and standings showdown. Slight favorite App State rides QB M. Singleton's 2,156-yard, 11-TD season plus RB J. Lewis's 8 rushing touchdowns. Home-standing Marshall answers with QB C. Del Rio-Wilson and WR X. Turner-Bradshaw's 4 TDs, pairing a stingy defense (40 passes defended) against App State's ball-hawking unit tallying 10 picks.

programme.title: Raptors vs Knicks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Kicking off a fierce new series at Scotiabank Arena, the visiting New York Knicks and Toronto Raptors reignite a heated NBA rivalry. New York carries a superior 6-5 record against the Raptors' 5-7 mark, entering as the clear favorites despite road inconsistencies. New York relies on the powerhouse pairing of J. Brunson's prolific 26.6 points and K. Towns' monstrous 13.7 rebounds and league-leading 12 double-doubles, while former Knick S. Barnes strikes back for Toronto with 23.5 points and a league-best 2.2 thefts per game. The Raptors lead the league in offensive rebounds and boast elite assist numbers, yet their prolific foul habit remains a critical flaw. This early-season clash is a massive test of the teams' shifting trajectories.

programme.title: Canucks at Golden Knights ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Vegas Golden Knights, leading the series 1-0, welcome the struggling Vancouver Canucks to T-Mobile Arena. VGK sit near the top of the NHL standings with a 13-5-2 record, while the Canucks have lost nine of their last ten. Jack Eichel (26 points) and Mark Stone (10 goals) power Vegas’ offense, but Vancouver’s Elias Pettersson (21 points) tries to spark a squad that ranks dead last in goals against (4.52 per game). These Pacific Division rivals meet again after Vegas took Game 1, hoping to extend their home dominance (7-3-1). VGK’s power play clicks at 27.4%, while VAN’s penalty kill is a league-worst 62.7%.

programme.title: 49ers at Cowboys ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the concrete savanna of AT&T Stadium, the dominant San Francisco 49ers, boasting a formidable 7-1 record and Brock Purdy's superb 109.8 rating, arrive to challenge the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys, underdogs on their home turf despite Dak Prescott's 16 touchdowns and CeeDee Lamb's 904 receiving yards, face their classic rivals in this NFL clash. The visitors, displaying superior form, are spearheaded by Christian McCaffrey's nine rushing scores, while the home side depends on J. Williams's ground game.

programme.title: Cavaliers vs Mavericks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Cleveland Cavaliers welcome the Dallas Mavericks to Rocket Arena for the series opener in this NBA clash. Cleveland's top-ranked offense (116.4 PPG, league-high 183 threes) contrasts with their 4-6 recent form, while Dallas arrives with a 6-4 run. Cooper Flagg (24.6 PPG, 6.5 APG) leads the visitors, and the Cavs counter with Donovan Mitchell (23.0 PPG) and Jarrett Allen's inside presence. With elite defensive rebounding and a strong assist game, Cleveland is favored at home, though both teams sit near .500.

programme.title: 76ers vs Pacers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Philadelphia 76ers, boasting a stellar 10-3 NBA record and riding a 7-3 run in their last ten, welcome the struggling Indiana Pacers (4-8, 3-7 in last ten) to Xfinity Mobile Arena for Game 2 of this series. PHI leads 1-0 after a previous meeting, and their league-leading offense (first in points, assists) is powered by Tyrese Maxey's 26.7 ppg and Joel Embiid's interior presence. The Pacers, paced by Pascal Siakam (22.4 ppg) and Andrew Nembhard's 7.6 assists, aim to even the series in front of a hostile Philadelphia crowd.

programme.title: Dukes vs Lakers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the Atlantic Union Bank Center, the James Madison Dukes, sitting at a 1-2 record after a tough start, face a Mercyhurst Lakers side winless on the road at 1-3 overall. The Lakers, though struggling offensively with a mere 61.3 points per game, boast a formidable defensive presence, tied for 34th in blocks and 23rd in steals, led by guard J. Lemelman who averages 16.8 points and 6.0 assists. Meanwhile, the Dukes, anchored by guard B. Lee’s 17.0 points per game, will aim to exploit their 39.2% field goal shooting at the Atlantic Union Bank Center, a venue where they have yet to secure a win this season. This national clash, with both teams seeking to improve their standing in NCAA Men’s Basketball, sees Mercyhurst’s aggressive defense go head-to-head with a home side hungry for its first victory on familiar hardwood.

programme.title: Lakers vs Hornets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The surging Lakers, boasting a 9-2 record atop the West, welcome the struggling Hornets to crypto.com Arena as this new series ignites; Los Angeles paces the league with 121.9 points per game, a dominant stat fueled by Luka Doncic’s staggering 39.3 PPG average, while Charlotte, languishing at 3-7 and 30th in scoring, must counter Walker Kessler’s interior presence and league-best offensive rebounding. The purple and gold have won eight of ten entering this clash, sitting comfortably near the conference summit, but the Hornets’ 52.7 rebound rate could exploit a Laker squad ranked 29th in total boards. An iconic non-conference rivalry adds extra juice to this marquee matchup at the iconic LA venue.

programme.title: Southend United vs Boreham Wood ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: Boreham Wood's flawless campaign invades Roots Hall as the English Conference's undefeated leaders collide with Southend United. The visitors boast an imposing 14-2-0 record, massive +27 goal differential, and stingy 17 goals conceded, contrasting the Shrimpers' 8-5-3 mark and +11 diff at home. Southend leans on ace L. Chambers-Parillon (8 goals) and clinical P. Omochere (6 in 6), but M Rush's 10 in just 7 outings and playmaker Z Brunt's 7 assists make the Wood heavy favorites to continue their streak on enemy turf. Southend's D Oldaker and V Daley-Campbell serve suspensions, while Boreham Wood welcome back R. Booty from a red card, sharpening their rivalry edge.

programme.title: Chargers at Ravens ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The winless Chargers, stumbling at 0-8 under the NFL's worst scoring offense (15.1 PPG) and a league-worst -7 turnover differential, travel to M&T Bank Stadium to face a Baltimore Ravens squad clawing back to .500 at 4-5. The Ravens ground game, fueled by Derrick Henry’s 689 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, clashes with a Chargers defense that's generated 7 interceptions but can't overcome Justin Herbert's 11 picks. Baltimore's Lamar Jackson owns a sparkling 118.4 passer rating, while the Chargers' O-line has allowed a staggering 31 sacks, a key vulnerability against a Ravens defense that has forced 17 sacks and 9 takeaways. This historic AFC rivalry sees the home team Ravens desperate to improve their 1-3 home record, with special note of Justin Tucker's clutch 64-yard field goal making him a weapon in a matchup where Baltimore seeks to exploit Los Angeles's 8 fumbles lost.

programme.title: Predators at Sharks ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Nashville Predators, apex hunters boasting an 11-4-5 record and dominant 8-1-1 recent form, venture into the San Jose Sharks’ SAP Center. The Sharks, languishing at 9-11-2, cling to their 1-0 series lead. San Jose’s defense, ranking first in NHL saves, revolves around Macklin Celebrini's eight goals. Nashville counters with a peerless penalty kill, orchestrated by Roman Josi (21 assists) and Steven Stamkos (11 goals). This pivotal home-ice clash deepens their fierce rivalry.

programme.title: Clippers vs Hornets ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The LA Clippers host the Charlotte Hornets at the new Intuit Dome to open their two-game series, both sides desperate to climb from sub-.500 records. The Clippers (2-8) boast a top-five offense behind Darius Garland (20.7 PPG) and Brook Lopez (14.7 PPG), while Charlotte (4-8) counters with the league’s best rebounding rate, led by Brandon Miller (20.6 PPG) and Naz Reid (17.2 PPG). The Hornets’ turnover woes play into LAC’s hands, ranking third in steals.

programme.title: Redhawks vs Bengals ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: At the Redhawk Center, the Seattle U Redhawks, boasting a sharp 50.9% field goal efficiency, host the winless Idaho State Bengals, who have stumbled to an 0-3 start on the road. The Bengals, struggling with a 35.3% shooting clip, lean heavily on guard M. Morris and his 18.0 points per game to ignite their offense. In stark contrast, the Redhawks counter with a balanced scoring attack led by W. Heimbrodt, who also anchors the defense with 2.0 blocks per game. This NCAA men’s basketball clash sees Seattle seeking to improve their 1-1 home record, while their guests aim for a breakthrough performance.

programme.title: Oilers at Flyers ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The NHL-leading Edmonton Oilers, boasting a scorching 14-3-3 record and a dominant 7-0-1 road mark, aim to extend their series lead over the Philadelphia Flyers to 2-0 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Connor McDavid, who has already amassed a staggering 49 points, drives an offense that leads the league in goals, while the Flyers, languishing in the basement at 5-10-6, counter with rookie phenom Matvei Michkov and his team-best 10 goals. Philadelphia’s defense blocks the most shots in the league yet owns the worst goal differential, a glaring issue against Edmonton’s red-hot power play, which converts at a stellar 33.3%.

programme.title: Panthers at Stars ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: In the American Airlines Center, a compelling NHL series continues for the structured Dallas Stars against the visiting Florida Panthers, a whirlwind of league-leading penalty minutes and hits. The Stars rely on superb form, epitomized by goalie Oettinger and his milestone four shutouts. Their faceoff dominance meets the Panthers' raw aggression in this absorbing rivalry. The home favorites aim to maintain their aggregate standing over such vibrant, undisciplined chaos.

programme.title: Bears vs Bobcats ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: The Montana State Bobcats, riding a scorching 9-1 record and sitting pretty atop the Big Sky Conference, roll into Nottingham Field to face a struggling Northern Colorado Bears squad that has dropped to 3-7 overall. MTST’s explosive offense, averaging a blistering 40.5 points per game behind QB Jordan Lamson’s 14 TDs and just one pick, sets up a brutal mismatch for a UNCO defense that’s been gashed for 382 yards per contest at home. The Cats’ 4-1 road form and plus-5 turnover margin look daunting for the Bears, who have lost five of six league games but boast J. Guin’s 588 rushing yards and five scores as a lone bright spot, while Lamson’s favorite target C. Dahlke (702 yards, 5 TDs) highlights a passing attack that ranks second in completion percentage at 71.2%.
